case_name: Robert O. Edwards, Jr. v. Douglas A. Collins
court: United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims

issues.label: Constructive possession of NAS reports
issues.why: The court must decide whether NAS Update 2010 and 2012 were constructively in the record before the AOJ's decision under the constructive-possession doctrine.

issues.label: Direct review docket evidentiary limits
issues.why: Whether 38 U.S.C. § 7113(a) barred the Board from considering Update 2012 depends on whether it was 'evidence of record' at the time of the AOJ decision.

issues.label: NAS report as evidence vs. argument
issues.why: The court must determine whether Update 2012's contents function as new evidence or merely as legal/factual argument the Board could consider.

issues.label: Duty to assist—medical examination trigger
issues.why: Whether the low McLendon/§ 5103A(d)(2) threshold indicating a possible nexus was met so as to require VA to furnish an exam.

issues.label: Biological mechanism theory sufficiency
issues.why: Whether the infection/immune-alteration theory in NAS reports suffices to indicate a possible nexus warranting an exam.

issues.label: Whether Update 2010 was of record
issues.why: Update 2010 was referenced via the April 2015 decision, raising whether it was properly before and considered by the Board and AOJ.

issues.label: AOJ failure to consider NAS reports
issues.why: The AOJ decisions noted no consideration of NAS reports, raising whether the duty to assist and review was satisfied.

issues.label: AOJ non-discussion of duty to assist
issues.why: The AOJ never addressed § 5103A, raising whether the duty-to-assist analysis was adequately performed.

issues.label: Board's reasons or bases adequacy
issues.why: The court must assess whether the Board gave adequate reasons or bases for denying an exam and distinguishing the prior decisions.

issues.label: Nonprecedential nature of prior Board decisions
issues.why: Under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1303, prior Board decisions are only persuasive, and the court must evaluate how the Board treated them.

issues.label: Board's distinguishing of April 2015 decision
issues.why: Whether the Board reasonably distinguished the tongue-carcinoma decision, including its silence on Update 2010.

issues.label: Board's distinguishing of September 2015 decision
issues.why: Whether distinctions based on absent private opinion and sunlight exposure were adequately reasoned.

issues.label: Dismissal of March 2018 decision
issues.why: Both parties agree the earlier-effective-date decision was correctly dismissed, but the court should confirm its irrelevance.

issues.label: Direct service connection elements
issues.why: The merits require applying the Washington v. Nicholson elements since presumptive service connection is unavailable.

issues.label: Absence of presumptive service connection
issues.why: The court must confirm squamous cell carcinoma is not listed under § 3.309(e), foreclosing presumptive service connection.

issues.label: Benefit of the doubt / equipoise
issues.why: Whether the evidence reaches equipoise triggering the benefit-of-the-doubt rule must be considered.

issues.label: Scope of remand relief
issues.why: Whether the appropriate remedy is remand to consider NAS reports and furnish an exam, and the terms of that remand.

issues.label: Standard of review for Board findings
issues.why: The court must apply the correct clearly-erroneous and arbitrary/capricious standards to the Board's determinations.

issues.label: Prejudicial error analysis
issues.why: Whether any Board or AOJ error was prejudicial to Mr. Edwards's claim must be assessed before remand.

issues.label: AMA docket election consequences
issues.why: The court must analyze how Mr. Edwards's election of the direct review docket constrains the record and available arguments.
